hints: Substitute $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ into the fraction $\frac{\tan x + \sin x}{\tan x - \sin x}$.
Factor out $\sin x$ from both numerator and denominator and simplify.
walkthrough:
Substitute $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ into the numerator and denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \sin x}{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} - \sin x}$$

Factor out $\sin x$ from both numerator and denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin x\left(\frac{1}{\cos x} + 1\right)}{\sin x\left(\frac{1}{\cos x} - 1\right)} = \frac{\frac{1 + \cos x}{\cos x}}{\frac{1 - \cos x}{\cos x}} = \frac{1 + \cos x}{1 - \cos x}$$

Equate to $k$ to complete the proof:
$$\frac{1 + \cos x}{1 - \cos x} = k$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Substitutes $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ (M1). Simplifies correctly to show $\frac{1 + \cos x}{1 - \cos x} = k$ (A1).

hints: Multiply across by $(1 - \cos x)$: $1 + \cos x = k(1 - \cos x)$.
Collect terms involving $\cos x$ on one side and make $\cos x$ the subject.
walkthrough:
Clear the fraction from $\frac{1 + \cos x}{1 - \cos x} = k$:
$$1 + \cos x = k(1 - \cos x) = k - k\cos x$$

Collect all terms involving $\cos x$ on one side:
$$\cos x + k\cos x = k - 1 \implies \cos x(k + 1) = k - 1$$

Divide by $(k + 1)$ to isolate $\cos x$:
$$\cos x = \frac{k - 1}{k + 1}$$

ai_rubric.Rearranging Formulas: Rearranges $1 + \cos x = k(1 - \cos x)$ (M1). Isolates $\cos x = \frac{k - 1}{k + 1}$ (A1).

hints: Substitute $k = 4$ into $\cos x = \frac{k - 1}{k + 1}$ to get $\cos x = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$.
Solve for $x$ in the interval $-\pi < x < \pi$.
walkthrough:
Substitute $k = 4$ into the formula for $\cos x$:
$$\cos x = \frac{4 - 1}{4 + 1} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$

Solve for all values of $x$ in the range $-\pi < x < \pi$:
$$x = \pm\cos^{-1}(0.6) \approx \pm 0.927\text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } \pm 0.295\pi)$$
